title: 3-query locally decodable codes: beat the cubic lower bound
premise_risks: Lean statement needs care with the order of quantifiers (c absolute, K depending on delta, eps)
plain: A 3-query locally decodable code encodes k bits into n bits so that any single message bit can be recovered with probability 1/2+eps by reading just 3 randomly chosen positions, even after a delta fraction of the codeword has been corrupted. The shortest known such codes have length exp(exp(O(sqrt(log k loglog k)))), while the best lower bound (2023) is n >= k^3/polylog(k). Prove n >= k^{3+c} for some fixed c>0.
math: A map $E:\{0,1\}^k\to\{0,1\}^n$ is a $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-LDC if for each $i\in[k]$ there is a probability distribution $\mu_i$ on pairs $(S,f)$ with $S\in[n]^3$ and $f:\{0,1\}^3\to\{0,1\}$ such that for all $x\in\{0,1\}^k$ and all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(y,E(x))\le\delta n$: $\Pr_{(S,f)\sim\mu_i}[f(y_S)=x_i]\ge\tfrac12+\varepsilon$. Prove: for all fixed $\delta,\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ there exist $c=c(\delta,\varepsilon)>0$ and $K$ such that every $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-LDC with $k\ge K$ has $n\ge k^{3+c}$. (Strengthening: $c$ independent of $\delta,\varepsilon$.)
